title: Tidepool atlas
story: A whole coast in a few square feet. Follow the water between jewel pools, pebbles, algae and invented sea creatures.
alt: Original imagined tide pools filled with colorful sea life, water and varied coastal stones.
challenge: Color islands and recognizable organisms give several easy starting points; water reflections add a gentle final stretch.
print: Preserve separation between turquoise water and dark rock. Check fine organisms at actual piece size, and keep key creatures away from trim.
pilot: Strong first proof candidate: accessible scene with multiple footholds.

title: Night greenhouse
audience: Plant lovers; people who enjoy an evening table ritual
story: The garden keeps its lights on. Warm windows, unusual foliage and quiet glass reflections make a little shelter after dark.
alt: An original glowing greenhouse at blue hour with many different leaves, pots and warm windows.
challenge: Architectural lines help establish the frame; foliage texture increases the challenge inside.
print: Shadow detail is the risk. Soft-proof blues and greens, then check a matte physical sample under household lighting.
pilot: Compare a 500-piece version with the proposed 750 before choosing.

title: The quiet terminal
story: There is time before departure. An invented spaceport offers plants, small travelers, distant stars and a place to sit.
alt: Original imaginary spaceport waiting hall with silhouettes, plants and cosmic light through large windows.
challenge: Big window geometry creates structure; quiet sky regions make this the slowest part of the journey.
print: Avoid turning subtle gradients into flat bands. A larger print master and clear differences across sky zones are required.
lesson: Narrative landmarks and large quiet regions
pilot: A later release; test whether sky area makes 1,000 pieces too demanding.

title: Saturday market
audience: Food lovers; families sharing an adult puzzle
story: A small town is made by its market. Follow produce, baskets, bicycles and bright canopies through an invented Saturday morning.
alt: Original colorful illustrated coastal farmers market with stalls, produce, bicycles and textiles.
challenge: Distinct stalls give several people independent sections to work on, then a shared finish.
print: Keep produce clusters readable and simulated print texture subtle. Small marks must not become muddy at final size.
pilot: Pair with The long table for a community collection.

title: Cloud observatory
audience: Dreamers; adults who prefer a shorter session
story: Somewhere above the weather, people measure clouds with improbable orange instruments. An impossible place with a welcoming map.
alt: Original whimsical weather laboratory on pastel sky islands with warm orange instruments and clouds.
challenge: Pastel shapes, architecture and warm landmarks support a lower piece count. Similar clouds still need deliberate contrast.
print: Pale tones can disappear on uncoated stock. Require a physical proof; refine cloud boundaries and minimum feature scale.
lesson: Lower piece counts without losing imagination
pilot: First large-piece study; size and handling need real user testing.

title: Workshop of small wonders
story: A cutaway workshop turns raw material into possibility. Benches, tools, molds and scraps form an invented community of making.
alt: Original detailed imagined community workshop with benches, hand tools, materials and small fabrication stations.
challenge: Different workstations form separate puzzle zones; many small details reward repeat looking.
print: Keep the scene illustrative, not a machinery instruction. Test tool-scale detail and eliminate accidental tiny marks in the print master.
lesson: Design for assembly; design for manufacture
pilot: Complement to Buildworks: a puzzle about making, not a competing small-object catalog.

title: A thousand little suns
story: Sunlight becomes a paper mosaic. Ochre, cobalt, peach and mint make a rhythm you can assemble one small interval at a time.
alt: Original geometric paper-textured mosaic of varied sun and wave shapes in ochre, cobalt, peach and mint.
challenge: Repeating motifs are intentionally harder. Different sizes and texture bands should prevent every piece looking alike.
print: Check saturated color clipping and repeated shape ambiguity. Consider 500 pieces if playtesting exposes too many false fits.
pilot: A specialist concept; do not assume every customer wants 1,000 pieces.

title: The long table
audience: Hosts; food and ceramic enthusiasts; shared tables
story: An overhead feast of vegetables, bowls, linens and hands. There is a place for another person at the table.
alt: Original overhead vegetarian feast with colorful food, ceramics, linens and anonymous hands.
challenge: Bowls and food provide obvious anchors. The cloth adds a modest quieter section without dominating the image.
print: Inspect generated hands and utensils, correct any anatomy or merged details in a final master, and proof food tones without oversaturation.
pilot: Test tactile piece handling and contrast with voluntary adult participants.

title: Library of tides
story: The library faces the sea. Shelves, stairs and little lamps hold a thousand imagined stories while the tide turns outside.
alt: Original intricate cross-section of a seaside library with colorful bookshelves, stairs, lamps and ocean windows.
challenge: Dense architecture supports extended solving, though repeated shelves require deliberate local variation.
print: 1,500 is a proposal, not a validated die. Require a much larger master, detail cleanup and an actual-size proof before sampling.
pilot: An advanced edition after demand and print detail have been tested.

title: After the rain
audience: Street photographers; people who like quiet cinematic scenes
story: The street shines after a coastal shower. Reflections, bicycles and warm windows turn an ordinary invented neighborhood into a small event.
alt: Original cinematic imagined wet coastal street with colorful puddle reflections, gardens, bicycles and warm windows.
challenge: Reflections connect upper and lower sections; garden textures and windows keep the dark pavement from becoming one uniform field.
print: Proof dark pavement carefully. Lift blocked shadows without flattening the evening atmosphere; check edges at the intended crop.
pilot: A 500-piece visual balance candidate after shadow proofing.
